models.model_label: Annual cross-sectional estimation of firm-year C_Score and G_Score (Equation 4; Table 3)
models.sample_description: CRSP–Compustat firm-years from 1963–2005 (115,516 observations in aggregate; 1962 is lost because lagged market value is required). The source excludes firm-years with missing estimation data, negative total assets or book equity, share price below $1, and annual top/bottom 1% of earnings, returns, size, market-to-book, leverage or depreciation. The model is estimated in annual cross-sections; exact N for any annual fit is not reported.
models.method_reported: Annual cross-sectional (Fama–MacBeth) regressions of earnings on the Equation (4) variables
models.method_details: The paper reports annual cross-sectional regressions and Fama–MacBeth means/t-statistics across 43 years, but does not identify the underlying estimator within each year.

dependent_variable.name: Earnings (X_i)
dependent_variable.definition: Earnings is the dependent variable X_i in Equation (4). Table 3 states that it is scaled by lagged price; Table 1 and Appendix A define earnings as net income before extraordinary items (Compustat data 18) scaled by lagged market value of equity, with Appendix A identifying market value as data 25 multiplied by data 199. These scaling statements conflict in the source, and the paper does not reconcile them.

evidence.quote: dependent variable is earnings scaled by lagged price
Earnings is net income before extraordinary items, scaled by lagged market value of equity.
Earnings is net income before extraordinary items (Compustat data18), scaled by lagged market value of equity

AppendixA prints Earnings as net income before extraordinary items(Compustat data18) scaled by lagged market value of equity(data25 x data199). The operator between data25 and data199 is multiplication.

Source-first selection: the authors describe estimation of a firm-year C_Score as the paper’s first objective and the methodology contribution. The retained baseline is the actually estimated annual cross-sectional Equation (4), reported in Table 3; Equations (2) and (3) are explicitly not separate regression models. C_Score validations, applications, later hypotheses and event studies are outside the construction-model family.

The Table 3 heading states that the dependent earnings measure is scaled by lagged price, while Table 1 and Appendix A define Earnings as net income before extraordinary items scaled by lagged market value of equity (Appendix A gives data25 multiplied by data199). The source does not reconcile these descriptions; formula is null and the conflict is preserved.

The paper reports annual Fama–MacBeth coefficient summaries but does not name the underlying estimator in each cross-section. The 115,516 firm-years are aggregate across 43 annual regressions; per-fit N is null.
